newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Troops man Zaire capital hotspots, block protest.
newsitem.headline: Troops man Zaire capital hotspots, block protest.

text.p: Hundreds of soldiers manned opposition hotspots in Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Friday after dispersing opposition militants trying to gather for a march in the city centre.

Witnesses said the secretary-general of the radical Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party, Adrien Phongo, was beaten and arrested by soldiers from the civil guard. The UDPS has called for talks with rebels advancing in the east.

Armed units of the Civil Guard were stationed at corners all along the route of a planned UDPS march, which was due to leave the central train station. Only a few dozen would-be marchers succeeded in reaching the departure point.
Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo's spokesman, Pascale Dema, said troops had been deployed to prevent the march, called in defiance of last month's government ban on all demonstrations.
Laurent Mbayo, a senior adviser of UDPS leader Etienne Tshisekedi, said the march was organised to demand negotiations between Tshisekedi, rebel leader Laurent Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko.
UDPS militas in the working class Matonge district said they planned to march to demand the resignation of Kengo and Mobutu.
